title: Body Language!
summary: Josh and Chuck examine body language: whether it is real or junk science, the myth that lack of eye contact signals deception, Albert Mehrabian's widely misquoted 7-38-55 percentages claim, the evolutionary roots of nonverbal communication, Nalini Ambady's "thin slices" research, innate versus learned versus hybrid gestures, cultural differences in gestures (eye contact, nodding, thumbs up, the "come here" gesture), five categories of nonverbal communication (emblems, illustrators, regulators, adapters, affect displays), Joe Navarro's FBI-based views on shoulders and victim selection, the dangers of applying body language in law enforcement and Paul Ekman's FACS, mirroring techniques, and the "baseline" concept. The episode closes with a listener mail about handling dark topics on the show, and a sign-off.
topics: emblems illustrators regulators adapters affect displays

segments.title: Opening banter and tour plug
segments.summary: Hosts plug live shows and the Warmer Climes winter tour, then introduce the episode on body language as a social science topic.

segments.title: Is body language real or junk science?
segments.summary: Hosts debate whether body language is scientifically valid, discussing the eye contact myth, habitual liars and psychopaths, the right-up-or-left-up lying myth, and the danger of using body language as forensic evidence.

segments.title: Mehrabian's 7-38-55 claim
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Albert Mehrabian's claim that facial expressions and tone of voice account for most of a first impression, and why the precise percentages are doubtful.

segments.title: Evolutionary origins of body language
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the John Napier quote on language and gestures, and how body language predates spoken language, including its survival role in judging approaching strangers and the Neanderthal question.

segments.title: Break and tangent
segments.summary: Mid-episode break followed by a casual tangent about bread ends and carving stations, and some banter about the hosts' high schools.

segments.title: Thin slices and gut instinct
segments.summary: Discussion of Nalini Ambady's thin slices research: snap judgments from the first seconds of meeting someone, linked to the limbic system and emotion, and how context and gut feelings relate to body language.

segments.title: Innate, learned, and hybrid body language; cultural differences
segments.summary: Hosts distinguish innate gestures like blushing and facial disgust from learned gestures like the middle finger, and hybrid gestures like shrugging. They cover culturally specific meanings of smiling, eye contact, thumbs up, peace sign, nodding, and calling a waiter.

segments.title: Five categories of nonverbal communication
segments.summary: Hosts walk through emblems, illustrators, regulators, adapters, and affect displays, with examples such as the middle finger, head shaking, looking at a watch, fidgeting, and facial expressions of emotion.

segments.title: Misreading cues, Ekman's FACS, and Joe Navarro on shoulders
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how easily body language is misread, the dangers of applying Paul Ekman's Facial Action Coding System in law enforcement, and FBI veteran Joe Navarro's views on shoulders, posture, and what criminals look for in victims. Also covers mirroring techniques and the advice of coaches, and the importance of a person's baseline behavior.
